subject: Segregated inference readout — decisions & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Brown <maya.brown@novushealth.com>, security-lead@novushealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Segregated inference readout — decisions & next steps

Hi Maya / Security team,

Thanks again for the time this morning — appreciated the deep context on your regulatory boundaries and the enclave constraints. Quick recap from our side, plus a proposed set of next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of pain & goals (what you confirmed)
- Data residency: all inference processing and logs must remain in EU-based VPCs; no persistent copy permitted outside EU.
- Air-gapped enclave: production inference cannot initiate outbound connections except to a small, whitelisted set of control endpoints; no public internet egress from compute nodes.
- Control plane: you prefer a private control plane (customer-managed) rather than Redwood-hosted control plane for production.
- KMS: customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) required for model keys and token encryption.
- Audit & retention: immutable audit logs retained for 90 days; sampling-level telemetry exported to your SIEM via approved collector.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile sub-350ms for 512-token requests within EU region (pilot target).

Open technical constraints we captured
- Egress model: only TLS to whitelisted IPs (will provide allowlist).
- No shared NFS mounts across administrative boundary — must use per-tenant volumes.
- Outbound DNS must be handled by your VPC resolvers; no split-horizon lookups to public resolvers.
- Pen test and SOC2 evidence required before go-live.

Attachments: discovery-notes-20261007.pdf (short notes), please see sections 2/3 for port/egress assumptions.

Proposed next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Novus: confirm whether private control plane in your VPC is mandatory or preferred for pilot — reply by 2026-10-13 (Maya).
2) Redwood: provide a succinct port+egress allowlist and a private-control-plane architecture diagram — by 2026-10-09 (Olga).
3) Procurement: Ben to share procurement path and required commercial documents; redlines/contract timeline goal — by 2026-10-12 (Ben).
4) Tech deep-dive: 60-90 minute on-call with your NetOps and our infra team to validate connectivity & routing (aim for week of 2026-10-18).

If any of the technical bullets above are inaccurate, please flag them inline and I will revise.

Best,

Subject: Re: Segregated inference readout — decisions & next steps

Aditya — thanks for the tidy recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Private control plane: Mandatory for production. For the pilot we can accept a temporary managed control plane if it’s fully isolated inside our VPC with no egress to Redwood-managed endpoints.
- Egress/allowlist: we can only permit outbound TLS to specified CIDR ranges; all traffic must be logged and sent to our collector (we run Splunk).
- KMS: HSM-backed KMS is non-negotiable for secrets at rest.
- SOC2 / pen test: we’ll need SOC2 Type II and an attestation that Redwood’s runtime will be included in the scoping for the pen test or a joint pen test plan.

Timeline note: security is pushing to have a pilot signed by the end of calendar Q4 (targeting mid-December). If procurement can move quickly we may accelerate.

One ask: can Redwood provide an architecture sketch showing how the private control plane would be deployed inside our VPC and what minimal egress is required (for telemetry, licensing heartbeat, etc.)? That will help my NetOps team decide what they can approve.

Quoted for visibility: your summary above.

— Maya
Maya Brown
Head of Information Security

Hi all — quick technical follow-up and a first-draft allowlist. I attached a compact network diagram and the CSV allowlist for your NetOps folks. 

Key clarifications from infra perspective:
- Private control plane model: we propose a small control-plane cluster deployed in your EU VPC (customer-managed subnets). Control plane communicates with inference nodes over an internal VPC endpoint; no public internet routes required.
- Heartbeat/telemetry: minimal egress required to 3 endpoints (TLS, outbound only via your NAT gateway). We can replace heartbeat with an agent that writes to an S3 bucket in your account if that is preferred.
- Ports: 443 for API/telemetry; 22 is not required (we rely on remote management agents); a separate port 20443 is used for mTLS peer connections between control plane and runtime (we can tunnel over 443 if your policy forbids new ports).

Proposed immediate actions:
- Aditya / Novus: schedule the 60-minute NetOps deep-dive next week (I’m available Wed/Thu mornings PT).
- Novus NetOps: accept novus-port-allowlist.csv and confirm if NAT-based outbound with your NAT + security groups is acceptable.
- Redwood: prepare private-control-plane diagram on Confluence and a short one-pager on our joint pen test approach.

Attachment stubs: novus-infra-highlevel.png, novus-port-allowlist.csv
